findings.finding: The new eaves-line wind girders, and the existing roof bracing strips, have no struts at their nodes. A horizontal girder spanning ~80 m along x needs chord/strut members along x at y = 0.0 and y = 3.68 (grid 2) and at y = 47.87 and 51.55 (grid 4). In the model the only x-direction members are purlins on their own 2.5 m spacing, which miss the brace nodes by up to 1.27 m. No eaves strut or tie exists at either edge (eaves_tie_depth is in params but no member is generated). As modelled, the girder panels and strip bracing cannot form complete triangulated load paths, so the long-face wind path from iter-01 B-STR-02 is still incomplete.
findings.evidence: Brace-node y vs nearest purlin y (reviewer's script on model/blender_manifest.json): 0.0 -> 0.24 m, 3.682 -> 0.84, 7.364 -> 0.30, 29.457 -> 0.49, 36.821 -> 0.75, 44.186 -> 1.01, 47.868 -> 0.13, 51.55 -> 1.27; purlin lines at y -10.73, -8.19, ..., 0.24, 1.98, 4.52, ..., 50.28; e.g. STR-BRACE-ROOF-EAVES2-BC-073 (8.0, 0.0) -> (16.0, 3.68); src/layout.py structure() generates no x-direction strut along grids 2 and 4
findings.fix: Put the purlins on the truss panel points: half-panels of 1.84 m (panel 3.68 m) suit sheeting and make every brace node a purlin/strut node. Alternatively add dedicated eaves struts (CHS or angle) along grids 2 and 4 and struts at ypan[1] / ypan[-2]. Then confirm the girder reactions reach the end-wall vertical bracing: the side-wall braced bay 5 on lines A and L is one bay away from grid 4, so the end-truss chord must act as a collector.

findings.finding: Now that the main truss is simply supported, it carries the full span moment over 51.55 m (span grew from 50.1 m) with an unchanged 3.0 m parallel-chord depth, i.e. span/depth ~17.2. That is shallow for a long-span roof truss at concept stage, where deflection and uplift reversal are likely to govern. There is still no bottom-chord lateral restraint (fly braces/ties) for uplift.
findings.evidence: metrics truss_main_span 51.55; config structure.truss_depth 3.0; STR-TRUSS-F verticals 2.65 m clear; no bottom-chord restraint members in 30_STR_Bracing
findings.fix: Test a 3.5-4.0 m depth (the bottom chord at grid 2 is +6.0, above the +2.98 rear passage) or a slight camber/precamber allowance; reserve space for bottom-chord restraint at panel points.

findings.finding: The foyer rafters frame into the hall truss end at top-chord level rather than onto the grid-2 column. The rafter end (centre z 8.875, bottom ~8.58) sits ~2.75 m above the column cap (+5.82). The foyer reaction is therefore an eccentric load on the truss end vertical, and the connection must stay genuinely pinned or continuity (and its effects) returns. The foyer roof (y -12..0) also has no bracing, and the 80 m facade line of 0.40 m grid-1 columns has no stated x-direction stability.
findings.evidence: STR-BEAM-FOYER-F strut (40, -12.0, 7.83) -> (40, 0.0, 8.875), section 0.3 x 0.6; STR-COL-F2 top z 5.82; STR-COL-F1 top 7.53, 0.40 x 0.40; no STR-BRACE-* with y < 0
findings.fix: Show a seated or bolted pin bracket on the truss end post (or drop the rafter onto a corbel or the column cap); add one braced bay in the foyer roof plane or facade (e.g. bays A-B and K-L between grids 1 and 2), or state that the grid-1 columns cantilever.

findings.finding: Steel is still the dominant cost driver. By linear length B02 has 5,303 m (trusses 2,308 m / 627 members + purlins 2,000 m + bracing 995 m), plus 11 x 12 m foyer rafters: ~71% more than A's 3,106 m (A's purlins are understated; see A review A-STR-01). The roof grew to 6,705 m2 (+26% vs A). Offsets: 56 vs 76 columns, 140 vs 163 m3 of pad concrete, 4,279 vs 5,824 m2 of external wall, and 30,149 vs 49,768 m3 of hall air volume.

strengths: Main design-premise issue fixed: continuity over grid 2 released, simply supported 51.55 m trusses with separate 12 m foyer rafters, so no gravity hold-down at the facade.
True Pratt web orientation (diagonals in tension under gravity), checked from member endpoints.
A lateral concept for wind on the 80 m faces now exists (eaves-line bracing in every bay along grids 2 and 4) and is recorded in the assumptions (structure.iteration2).
Every column has a pad footing (56/56); clash matrix BLD-CLASH 0 clashes over 193,988 pairs, with positive and negative controls.

Envelope outside the column line, a single roof plane with no box gutters, a lower structure (roof top +14.32 vs A +18.4) and a larger gutter with more downpipes all help buildability and maintenance; open_issues now covers splices, erection and crane planning, the movement joint and gutter access.
limitations: No loads, rainfall, wind or geotechnical data are available, so adequacy, deflection and uplift cannot be judged; span/depth remarks are rules of thumb, not calculations. Read-only checks were run on model/blender_manifest.json (truss F nodes and diagonals, foyer rafter and column extents, gutter/canopy/roof extents, brace-node vs purlin alignment, column/footing counts), src/layout.py structure(), reports and comparisons/out/comparison.md. Renders in renders/B02-3c1014f7b9/ and the exports drawings were not inspected in detail. Crane availability in Zimbabwe was not verified.
certification_disclaimer: This review is a structured QA metric for a concept coordination model by an AI reviewer. It is not a professional engineering certification, structural design check, code-compliance statement, fire approval or cost estimate. No loads, analysis or member design were performed; all member sizes in the model are space-reservation placeholders. A registered Zimbabwean structural engineer must design and certify the structure.
